newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower on stocks, spillover.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower on stocks, spillover.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended lower on a reduced wheat ending stocks estimate by USDA and on spillover pressure from CBOT soybeans, traders said.

"It was a leaking market all day. There was no buying in the pit, then we saw some fund liquidation and that triggered stops," a MGE trader said. "There just weren't any friends for our market today."

All three U.S. wheat markets sagged lower after USDA raised its estimate of 1996/97 wheat ending stocks by five million bushels to 465 million. Some analysts had anticipated a cut of five to 10 million bushels.
Further pressure came from CBOT soybeans, which dropped sharply after USDA left unchanged its estimate for ending soybean stocks. The trade had been expecting a decrease.
Wheat traders also said their market was broadly lower amid calculations for estimated U.S. spring wheat production based on the report's estimate of total U.S. wheat production.

"Essentially you can come up with a spring wheat production number by taking the all-wheat estimate and subtracting out the various classes," a trader said. "The number comes up to be around 545 million bushels. That's certainly more bearish than people were thinking in March."
MGE spring wheat settled five to 16-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with July down 16-1/2 cents at $4.16-1/2. New crop September lost 14-1/2 cents to settle at $4.16-1/2.
Benson-Quinn was a featured player, selling two million July bushels but also buying 1.5 million July.
